extracted.intended_audience: parties to USITC Investigation No. 337-TA-1350 (Realtek v. AMD), interested government agencies, and other interested persons
extracted.subtask_short: USITC briefing on issues under review
extracted.subtask_description: Solicit and instruct written submissions in Investigation No. 337-TA-1350 on discrete issues under Commission review (claim construction, infringement, prior art, economic prong, sanctions) and on remedy, bond, and the public interest, including procedural requirements for filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit briefing to discrete issues requested
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties are invited to brief only the discrete issues requested in this notice. The parties are not to brief other issues on review, which are adequately presented in the parties' existing filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefs should address only the enumerated questions/issues under A–D; avoid re-briefing matters already adequately presented in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: '218 patent — metal-layer orientation/global power mesh (Issue A(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For claim 12, limitations 12[e] and [f], explain whether these limitations allow both horizontal and vertical power supply wires of the claimed 'global power mesh' to be on the same metal layer, and identify intrinsic evidence in support. For each accused AMD product, the asserted domestic industry products, and the asserted prior art references, explain whether the 'global power mesh' includes: (i) at least one metal layer in which all power supply wires on that layer are horizontal; and (ii) at least a second, different metal layer in which all power supply wires on that layer are vertical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite intrinsic record evidence and apply constructions used in the FID (see FID at 109–110, 117–118). Distinguish accused products and prior art feature-by-feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: '218 patent — local vs global power mesh distinction (Issue A(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to limitations 12[a]-[c], explain how intrinsic evidence distinguishes a 'first [partial] local power mesh' from a 'second [partial] local power mesh,' and how it distinguishes a 'global power mesh' from two local power meshes (e.g., whether different local power meshes must be insulated, comprise different wire networks, or have different power levels). For each accused product, asserted DI product, and prior art reference, explain whether that product/reference discloses two or more local power meshes and how it distinguishes a 'global power mesh' from two local power meshes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the basis on which images relied on in the FID identify two partial meshes vs. a single global power mesh; tie arguments to intrinsic claim language and record images.

rubrics_metrics.name: '218 patent — power domain distinction (Issue A(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to limitations 12[a]-[c], explain how intrinsic evidence distinguishes a 'first power domain' from a 'second power domain' (e.g., whether power domains must be insulated or have different power requirements, temporarily or at all times). For each accused product, asserted DI product, and asserted prior art reference, explain whether it discloses two or more power domains distinguished by that feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intrinsic/extrinsic evidence to show whether claim language requires different domains and how that affects infringement/invalidity/DI technical prong findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: '218 patent — meaning of 'provide the power needed' (Issue A(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain whether intrinsic evidence supports or precludes reading 'provide the power needed' in limitation 12[c] to include zero power or zero voltage. If 'power' could include zero power/zero voltage, explain whether that construction impacts the FID's findings on infringement, the technical prong of domestic industry, or invalidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss semantic construction and material impact on prior findings; consider hypothetical and record evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: '218/'582 patents — asymmetry of obviousness combinations (Issue A(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain whether and how claims 15–18 of the '582 patent can be invalid over Li with Jiang (as defined in the FID) but not over Jiang with Li.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze the teachings of each reference and whether order/combination materially affects obviousness conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: '218 patent — Jiang3 prior art status (Issue A(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain whether there is any evidence to rebut testimony that Jiang3 was publicly available prior to November 15, 2007, or that Jiang3 is not prior art to the '218 patent. Explain how Jiang3 relates to Jiang and Jiang2 and whether it contributes to the issue of obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentary or testimonial evidence regarding public availability dates and factual comparisons showing how Jiang3 bears on novelty/obviousness analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: '218 patent — PTAB challenge to Jiang3 (Issue A(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain whether Complainant has challenged the prior art status of Jiang3 in the currently pending PTAB proceeding IPR2023-00920 concerning the '218 patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain procedural posture and any differences between PTAB record and USITC record relevant to prior art status.

rubrics_metrics.name: '582 patent — capacitor component location and effect (Issue B(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to arrangement of the 'capacitor component' relative to the 'inductor component' in claim 1 of the '582 patent, explain whether 'a capacitor component' requires that substantially all capacitor components lie between the 'extension-conductor segments' that define the 'first region,' or whether there may be additional capacitor components outside those 'extension-conductor segments' (but not under the 'coil-conductor segment'), provided at least one capacitor component is in the 'first region.' Explain whether presence of capacitors outside extension-conductor segments tends to increase unwanted phase noise, parasitic circuits, or otherwise degrade the invention. Explain whether accused products and Qualcomm RFR1000 and RBR6122 contain at least one capacitor component substantially within the 'first region.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address both claim construction (scope of 'a capacitor component') and technical effects (phase noise/parasitics). Provide product-by-product comparisons to claim-defined 'first region.'

rubrics_metrics.name: '582 patent — difference between 'defined by' and 'defined between' (Issue B(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain whether there is any difference in claim construction or scope between 'wherein a first region is defined by the two extension-conductor segments' (claim 1, limitation 1[c]) and 'wherein the first region is defined between the two extension-conductor segments' (dependent claim 4). Explain whether/how Qualcomm RBR1000 reads on claim 1 but not claim 4 based on any difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any nuance in phrasing that affects claim scope and prior art application; show how dependent claim language narrows or does not narrow claim 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: '582 patent — electrode segments vs connecting segments (Issue B(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to Qualcomm RFR6122, explain whether claim 1 limitations 1[e], [f] cover an arrangement in which the 'electrode segments' can comprise the metal plates of one set of capacitors while the claimed 'connecting segments' belong to a different set of capacitors. Explain whether RFR6122 discloses a single set of capacitors (or 'capacitor component') that satisfies both 'electrode segments' and 'connecting segments.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed mapping of accused device structures to claim-elements and argue whether separate capacitor sets or a single set satisfy the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: '582 patent — Muh prior art/PTAB evidence (Issue B(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the arguments and evidence presented before PTAB concerning the prior art status of Muh in IPR2023-00788. How is the evidence before PTAB different from the record in this investigation? Should the Commission consider additional PTAB arguments/evidence at this stage? Based on the record and differing evidentiary standards, can the Commission reach a different conclusion than PTAB? (See Nobel Biocare Servs. AG v. Instradent USA, Inc., 903 F.3d 1365 (Fed. Cir. 2018)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast standards of proof and record scope; explain whether PTAB evidentiary presentations merit Commission consideration or remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: '582 patent — remand if Muh is prior art (Issue B(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission determines Muh qualifies as prior art, address whether a remand is appropriate to allow the ALJ to consider obviousness based on Muh in the first instance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss procedural fairness, record completeness, and whether ALJ analysis is required for Muh-based obviousness determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic prong — allocation of Broadcom investments (Issue C(13))
rubrics_metrics.description: For Broadcom's asserted labor and capital investments under 19 U.S.C. 1337(a)(3)(B) and (C), identify evidence of record that supports finding these investments were properly allocated to the asserted domestic industry products (Broadcom BCM4387 and BCM4389) and limited to investments in the United States directed to the asserted DI products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentary proof of allocation methodology, scope of U.S. activities, and linkage to asserted DI products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic prong — nexus between Realtek investments and patents (Issue C(14))
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify evidence of record supporting Realtek's contention that the requisite nexus exists between its asserted investments under 19 U.S.C. 1337(a)(3)(C) and the asserted patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to contracts, development activities, timelines, and other evidence tying investments to exploitation of asserted patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic prong — significance/substantiality of investments (Issue C(15))
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify evidence of record with respect to whether Realtek has shown that the investments upon which it relies are significant or substantial, per 19 U.S.C. 1337(a)(3)(B) and (C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify investments, compare to industry norms, and address materiality to domestic industry requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic prong — meaning of 'articles protected by the patent' (Issue C(16))
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the meaning of 'articles "protected by the patent"' in subsections 337(a)(2) and (a)(3) and whether that language requires Broadcom to hold a license to the asserted patents, or that the Broadcom BCM4387 and BCM4389 chips are otherwise protected by the asserted patents, for Realtek to rely on Broadcom's domestic investments to establish a domestic industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze statutory text and precedent to determine whether 'protected by the patent' requires license/ownership or can be satisfied by other relationships; explain implications for DI proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction — identification of outside counsel if sanction applied (Issue D(17))
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming the Commission affirms imposition of the monetary sanction but decides to impose it on Realtek's 'outside counsel' consistent with Realtek's petition, identify which 'outside counsel' would be subject to the sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide names/roles of outside counsel and record citations tying them to the sanctionable conduct as framed in the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant remedial submission contents
rubrics_metrics.description: In its initial submission, Complainant is requested to identify the remedy sought and to submit proposed remedial orders. Complainant is further requested to state the dates that the asserted patents expire, to provide the HTSUS subheadings under which the accused products are imported, and to supply identification information for all known importers of the products at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed remedial orders should be specific and include patent expiration dates, HTSUS codes, and known importer identities so Commission can draft enforceable orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting exclusion for non-consumption purposes — show adverse effects
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party seeks exclusion of an article from entry into the United States for purposes other than entry for consumption, the party should indicate that and provide information establishing that activities involving other types of entry either are adversely affecting it or likely to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide factual evidence showing harm from other types of entry (e.g., temporary importation, duty-free zones) and why exclusion is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service/repair exemption considerations for remedial orders
rubrics_metrics.description: If AMD requests that remedial orders contain an exemption related to service or repair, submissions should address: (i) factual rationale for providing such an exemption, including under public interest factors in section 337(d); (ii) the warranty terms, if any, for the merchandise; (iii) whether exemption should apply only to merchandise under warranty or to all needed service and repair; and (iv) the appropriate temporal cutoff for the exemption (e.g., issuance of Commission final determination or end of Presidential review period, and whether it should apply to merchandise sold/imported prior to such date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support exemption requests with evidentiary details (warranty terms, scope of repairs, public interest impacts) and propose concrete operative dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest factors to be addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will consider the effects of any remedy on: (1) public health and welfare; (2) competitive conditions in the U.S. economy; (3) U.S. production of articles like or directly competitive with those subject to investigation; and (4) U.S. consumers. Submissions should address these factors in context of the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor arguments to the four listed public interest factors, providing empirical or factual support where possible (market data, health/safety implications, domestic production impacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond submissions during Presidential review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission orders a remedy, the U.S. Trade Representative has 60 days to review; during that period covered articles would be entitled to enter the U.S. under bond in an amount determined by the Commission and prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury. The Commission is interested in receiving submissions concerning the amount of the bond that should be imposed if a remedy is ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide justification and methodology for bond amount (harm mitigation, estimated damages, scope of covered articles) and consider the practical effects during the Presidential review period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines for initial and reply written submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial written submissions and proposed remedial orders must be filed no later than close of business on June 28, 2024. Reply submissions must be filed no later than close of business on July 8, 2024. No further submissions on these issues will be permitted unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing is mandatory; late submissions will be subject to denial unless Commission orders otherwise (Realtek's late public interest statement was denied as example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening submissions are limited to 100 pages. Reply submissions are limited to 50 pages. No further submissions on any of these issues will be permitted unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure filings to fit within page limits; exhibits may be governed by confidentiality rules and filing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons filing written submissions must file the original document electronically on or before the deadlines. The Commission's paper filing requirements in 19 CFR 210.4(f) are currently waived. Submissions should refer to the investigation number (Inv. No. 337-TA-1350) prominently on the cover page/first page. See Handbook for Electronic Filing Procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EDIS/handbook procedures; contact the Secretary with filing questions. Ensure prominent investigation number placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential treatment and redaction procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person desiring to submit a document in confidence must request confidential treatment by marking each document with a header indicating that the document contains confidential information. This will satisfy Rules 201.6(b) and 210.5(e)(2). Any non-party wishing to submit comments containing confidential information must serve those comments on the parties pursuant to the applicable Administrative Protective Order. A redacted non-confidential version of the document must be filed with the Commission and served on parties within two business days of any confidential filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark confidential documents clearly; file a redacted public version within two business days to permit public inspection rights and compliance with protective order service requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and permitted uses of submitted information
rubrics_metrics.description: All information, including confidential business information and documents for which confidential treatment is properly sought, submitted to the Commission may be disclosed to and used: (i) by the Commission, its employees and Offices, and contract personnel (a) for developing/maintaining records of this or related proceedings, or (b) in internal investigations, audits, reviews, and evaluations; or (ii) by U.S. government employees and contract personnel, solely for cybersecurity purposes. All contract personnel will sign NDAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential submitters should be aware of limited disclosure channels and that contract personnel will sign nondisclosure agreements; cite specific statutory/administrative authorities if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of non-confidential submissions (EDIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: All non-confidential written submissions will be available for public inspection on EDIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan redactions accordingly; public versions will be made accessible and can be relied upon for public comment and discovery by third parties.
